before: written and committed before any tick was fetched for this study and before any rule ran on real data. Read before freezing: deriving.md section five, spiking.md, deriv-variants.md, generators.md, rebuilding.md, crash-timing.md, lrc-retest.md. Probes made: (1) the bridge serves M1 bars only from 2026-07-28, M5 from 2025-10-23, M15 from 2023-11-28 (the terminal's ~100k-bar cap) and H1/H4/D1 from 2019; it serves ticks from 2025-01-01 on all six indices (404 before; Range Break's tick store starts on the same day); (2) on the published 24 hours of research.db ticks (2026-09, already used by deriving.md) the grind is one-signed on all six: every bid move on the spike side is a spike (0.11% of Boom 1000 ticks, 1/rate), the smallest spike-side move is 3-20x the largest grind step. No rate, state or trend was computed on the study data.
question: Do Boom/Crash spikes move with the trend? Boom spikes up and Crash spikes down by design, so the spike direction is fixed per index; the question is whether the HAZARD (how often) or the SIZE of the spike differs when the trend read from closed bars before the spike points the spike's way (aligned), against it (counter), or nowhere (range). HTF 1h, 4h, 1d; LTF 1m, 5m, 15m (amended before the run, desk message of 2026-10-05); and multi-timeframe alignment.
indices: Boom 300, Boom 500, Boom 1000, Crash 300, Crash 500, Crash 1000 Index (the broker DB holds only Boom/Crash 1000 bars, so every index is fetched from the bridge). The spike direction s = +1 for Boom, -1 for Crash.

data.ticks: the lab's MT5 bridge, /symbols/ticks/{symbol}/range, read-only, one UTC day per request, at least 1.5 s apart, from 2025-01-01 to the last complete UTC day; stored as one npz per index-day (ms, bid, ask) under the study's own lab directory; never written to mt5bt.db
data.bars: bridge /symbols/rates/range H1, H4, D1 bid bars from 2019-01-01, used ONLY to warm up the full-series 1h/4h/1d indicators before the first tick day. From the first tick day on, every bar at every timeframe is built from the ticks' bids (1m OHLC from ticks; 5m/15m/1h/4h/1d resampled from 1m by UTC floor). A minute with no tick has no bar (as MT5).
data.swap: bridge /symbols/info swap_long / swap_short (swap_mode 5 = annual % of price, costs.md)
data.split: the tick history is shorter than the 2024-01-01 convention allows, so: discovery = the first half and confirmation = the second half of the span common to all six indices, cut at the UTC midnight nearest the midpoint (expected about 2025-11-17). Every cut, tercile and null parameter is fitted on discovery only.

spikes.tick move: d = log(bid[i]) - log(bid[i-1]) on consecutive ticks (bid, as MT5 bars; log units since the amendment of 2026-10-05)
spikes.grind step: a move against the spike side or zero: s*d <= 0
spikes.spike tick: s*d > theta, theta = 3 x the 99.9th percentile of |d| over discovery grind steps of that index
spikes.event: consecutive spike ticks merge into one spike; its time is the first spike tick's time, its size J = s*(log bid after the last spike tick - log bid before the first)
spikes.sub-threshold: spike-side moves 0 < s*d <= theta are counted and reported (expected about none); they are treated as grind
spikes.size units: primary: J / median J of that index's discovery spikes; secondary: J / ATR(14) of the full-series 1h bars at the last closed 1h bar

series.ex-spike: bid minus the cumulative sum of spike sizes (times s) since the first tick: the grind alone. Its bars are built the same way from the ex-spike ticks
series.registered expectation (from the probe,: because the grind is one-signed, the ex-spike series is monotone (Boom down, Crash up). Its LRC slope sign is then always counter to the spike, and its 3/3 pivots of one kind never form, so its MCFL state is constant. The ex-spike DIRECTION is therefore expected to be degenerate by construction: every spike counter to the ex-spike trend, no aligned spikes to compare. If on study data an index-timeframe's ex-spike direction puts < 1% of ticks in either state, its ex-spike direction cells are reported as degenerate and not tested. The ex-spike series still carries the grind RATE, so its strength readings (below) are tested.
series.what separates 'trend because of spikes': (1) every reading uses only bars closed before the minute being scored (causal), so a spike cannot be inside its own trend reading; (2) the fitted constant-hazard null runs through the identical pipeline: whatever relation it shows is mechanical; (3) the ex-spike series has no spikes in it; (4) a deliberately non-causal reading (S10: the trend of the bar that CONTAINS the spike) is reported to show how large the mechanical relation is when causality is dropped

trend readings, per timeframe tf in 1m 5.ATR: ATR(14), Wilder, of that tf's bars (lrc_retest.atr)
trend readings, per timeframe tf in 1m 5.LRC(100): least-squares line through the last 100 closes (lrc_retest.lrc): slope b per bar; Pearson R of the closes against bar index over the same 100 bars
trend readings, per timeframe tf in 1m 5.direction: aligned when s*b > 0, counter when s*b < 0 (b = 0 is neither and dropped)
trend readings, per timeframe tf in 1m 5.structure: MCFL v2 as lrc_retest.structure (3/3 pivots known 3 bars later, HH/HL/LH/LL with 0.1 ATR tolerance): state UP / DOWN / MIXED; aligned = UP on Boom, DOWN on Crash; counter = the opposite; range = MIXED
trend readings, per timeframe tf in 1m 5.strength: |b| / ATR and |R|; terciles WEAK / MID / STRONG cut per index x tf x series on discovery minutes
trend readings, per timeframe tf in 1m 5.range (LRC): the WEAK |R| tercile, whatever the sign
trend readings, per timeframe tf in 1m 5.ex-spike grind rate: ex-spike |b| / the index's discovery mean grind per bar of that tf; terciles on discovery
trend readings, per timeframe tf in 1m 5.known at: a tf bar opening at t closes at t + tf; its readings apply to every minute starting at or after t + tf until the next bar closes. Minute m is scored with the last tf bar closed at or before m's start, so the 1m reading for minute m is bar m-1

outcomes.hazard: spikes per tick in a state: (spikes in minutes in that state) / (ticks in those minutes). Reported also per minute and as P(>= 1 spike in the next 1 minute) and P(>= 1 spike in the next 15 minutes) (windows starting on 15-minute boundaries, the state at the window's start)
outcomes.hazard ratio: rate(aligned) / rate(counter); pooled across indices as an O/E ratio: (sum_i spikes_i,A / sum_i ticks_i,A x rate_i) / (same for counter), rate_i = the index's own rate over the half
outcomes.size: mean J / median J (discovery) by state; size ratio aligned / counter; P(J > 2 median J)
outcomes.published and measured constant hazard: the name's 1 / (300, 500, 1000) per tick, the measured discovery rate, and deriving.md's 267.7, 529.4, 908.3, 329.0, 507.7, 973.8 ticks per spike

nulls.fitted constant-hazard null (the matched: a compound-Poisson-jump-plus-grind tick simulator fitted per index on discovery ticks only: on the REAL tick timestamps, each tick is a spike with constant probability p = discovery spikes / discovery ticks; a spike's size is drawn iid from the discovery spike sizes; every other tick moves by a grind step drawn iid from the discovery grind steps (zeros included); spread = the real tick's spread at the same tick index. A 150-day warm-up at the median tick interval is simulated before the first tick so the 1d readings are live on day one. 40 paths per index. Every state, rate, ratio, tercile cut (re-fitted on the path's own discovery half), trade and plot is computed on each path by the identical code. In this null hazard and size are constant by construction, so any relation a reading shows on it is mechanical
nulls.positive control: the same simulator with the hazard multiplied by 1.25 and the jump size divided by 1.25 (amended before the run, see amended_before_run) while the path's own 4h full-series LRC(100) is aligned (state updated at each simulated 4h close); 4 paths per index; the pipeline must recover a primary ratio near 1.25, which shows the test has the power to see an effect of that size
nulls.matched walks: the desk's iid and GARCH Gaussian walks (mcfl/synth.py) have no spikes and are not a null for a hazard; they are used only for the trade question, matched to the 15m full-series bars

primary.requested and why it cannot be the prima: the desk asked for the aligned vs counter hazard ratio on the 4h EX-SPIKE trend. By the registered expectation above that ratio has no aligned spikes to put in its numerator. It is computed and reported first (the share of spikes aligned with the ex-spike 4h trend, expected 0%), and the primary moves to the full series, measured against the null that removes what spikes do to the trend
primary.P1: the aligned / counter spike hazard ratio, 4h full-series LRC(100) direction, the six indices pooled (O/E), confirmation half
primary.P1 passes when: log(real ratio) - mean over null paths of log(null ratio) has |z| >= 1.645 against the null paths' sd, AND the real ratio's day-bootstrap 90% interval (1000 draws, days resampled jointly across indices) excludes the null mean ratio, AND the discovery half shows the same sign. Otherwise the HTF trend does not move the spike hazard
primary.P2 (co-primary, multi-timeframe, amended: the hazard ratio HTF and LTF BOTH aligned / BOTH counter, HTF = 4h, LTF = 15m, full-series LRC(100) direction, six pooled (O/E), confirmation, same pass rule as P1
primary.both primaries: each judged on its own; Bonferroni is not applied between the two (both are reported with their z); the trade question opens only if P1 or P2 passes

secondaries (Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.S1 direction: aligned / counter hazard ratio by LRC sign, per index x tf (6) x series (full; ex-spike if not degenerate)
secondaries (Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.S2 structure: MCFL aligned / counter and range (MIXED) / (aligned or counter) hazard ratios, per index x tf x series
secondaries (Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.S3 strength: hazard ratio STRONG / WEAK tercile of |b|/ATR and of |R|, within aligned and within counter (full), per index x tf; ex-spike: STRONG / WEAK of |b|/ATR, |R| and the grind rate
secondaries (Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.S4 size: size ratio aligned / counter (J / median J) per index x tf x series; and by strength tercile; and J / ATR(1h) reported, not tested (ATR contains the spikes)
secondaries (Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.S5 next-window probabilities: P(spike in next 1m) and P(spike in next 15m) by state, reported against the constant-hazard value, not tested separately (monotone in the rate)
secondaries (Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.S6 alignment count (amended before the r: at each minute, the number of the six tf (1m 5m 15m 1h 4h 1d) whose full-series LRC(100) direction is aligned, 0-6; the slope of log hazard on the count (Poisson regression), per index and pooled; plus a strength-weighted score sum_tf (+1 aligned / -1 counter) x |R_tf|, hazard ratio top / bottom quintile (discovery cuts). Ex-spike version reported where not degenerate
secondaries (Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.S7 nested states (amended before the run: for every HTF in (1h 4h 1d) x LTF in (1m 5m 15m), full series: BOTH aligned, HTF aligned + LTF counter (pullback), HTF counter + LTF aligned, BOTH counter; tested: both-aligned / both-counter, pullback / both-aligned, and each state's rate / the index's rate, per index and pooled
secondaries (Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.S8 clustering: inter-arrival gap in ticks: CV against a geometric's sqrt(1-p); dispersion (variance / mean) of spike counts per 15m, 1h, 1d window; lag-1 autocorrelation of counts per minute and per 15m; each against the null paths; and gap CV and dispersion within aligned vs counter 4h states
secondaries (Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.S10 the mechanical relation, shown: the same ratios with the state read from the bar that CONTAINS the minute (non-causal, look-ahead by design), real and null, to show the size of 'trend because of spikes'; never a verdict

trade.sides: the spike side only: long Boom, short Crash
trade.entry: at each 15m full-series bar close: buy at the ask of the first tick at or after the close (Crash: sell at the bid); one entry per 15m close, trades may overlap
trade.variants: T-with: 4h full-series LRC(100) aligned at the last closed 4h bar; T-against: counter; T-all: unconditioned; also T-with-ex: 4h ex-spike grind rate in its STRONG tercile
trade.stop: structural: Boom: the lowest bid low of the last 3 closed 15m bars - 0.1 ATR(14, 15m); risk = max(entry - stop, 0.25 ATR); Crash mirrored with highs. Filled at the first bid at or beyond the stop (the grind side does not gap)
trade.exit: market-decided: at the first spike after entry, out at the bid of the tick after the last spike tick (the first price available after seeing it; Crash: the ask); else a 24-hour time stop at the bid (ask)
trade.R: s x (exit - entry) / risk, spread inside the prices (buy ask, sell bid); swap charged pro rata per second held at the bridge's annual rate; no commission (Deriv synthetics charge none); gross R also reported (bid to bid)
trade.report: mean R net with day-bootstrap 90% interval; P(R >= N) for N = 1, 2, 4, 10 against 1/(N+1) and against the same rule on the fitted null paths and on iid / GARCH walks matched to the 15m bars (walks: same entries, stop and a target-free hold to the 24-hour stop, spread in ATR units); per index and pooled; verdict for T-with vs T-against vs T-all only if P1 or P2 passed

kill conditions, written before the run: P1 fails: the 4h trend does not change how often a Boom/Crash spike comes
the positive control's recovered ratio is below 1.10 or its interval covers 1: the test cannot see an effect of 1.25, and a P1 failure is reported as underpowered, not as a null
the measured discovery rate is more than 15% away from deriving.md's tick-level rate: the spike detector is wrong and nothing downstream is read
the fitted null fails to reproduce the real gap CV and the real 1h dispersion within its own 90% band on discovery: the null is mis-specified and the S8 comparisons are withdrawn
amended_before_run: 2026-10-05, after a synthetic-only test of the code and before any real-data run: the positive control multiplies the hazard by 1.25 AND divides the jump size by 1.25 while the path's own 4h trend is aligned. Raising the hazard alone breaks the closure E[J] = lambda E[g]: the aligned state then has a positive drift, the trend feeds itself and on a 120-day synthetic path every 4h bar stayed aligned, leaving no counter state to compare. With the size scaled the drift stays zero and only the hazard changes (the size ratio the control shows is then 0.8 by construction).

2026-10-05, after an end-to-end run on SYNTHETIC constant-hazard data only (six fake indices, 60 days, 10 null paths) and before any real-data run: the frozen 'z against the null paths' used the paths' sd as if known, and on data that IS the null it produced 14 Benjamini-Hochberg survivors of 531 cells, because 10-40 paths estimate a sd noisily. The test is now predictive: z = (log real - mean log null) / (sd x sqrt(1 + 1/n)), sd = max(the paths' sd, the Poisson sd of a log rate ratio sqrt(1/s1 + 1/s2) for hazard cells), p two-sided from Student t with n - 1 df. On the same synthetic data: 0 survivors of 531, P1 z = +0.41, and the positive control recovered 1.21 (injected 1.25). The same z is used for P1 and P2.

2026-10-05, after the first real-data PREP of Boom 300 only (spike count and threshold, no trend reading looked at): the detector's threshold in price points (theta = 0.396) missed 11,610 small spikes and read 1 spike per 316 ticks. The cause is a unit error, not the process: the index is multiplicative - over the sample Boom 300 went from 715 to 4,359 and back to 1,055, and its grind step (99.9th pct 0.026 to 0.147 points) and smallest spikes (5th pct 0.11 to 0.86 points) scaled with the price, so a fixed point threshold sits inside the spike distribution at low prices. Every tick move, theta, the spike size J and the null simulator (grind and jump draws, applied multiplicatively) are now in log-price units; size in ATR uses the price jump. Spike-side moves of any size give 1 per 289-300 ticks in every quarter of Boom 300, against deriving.md's 267.7 from one 24-hour window. The first output was set aside unread as out_v0_absolute_theta.
